newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast crudes ease with WTI, static ANS.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast crudes ease with WTI, static ANS.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crudes edged down in line with lower West Texas Intermediate crude (WTI) and static spot trade for Alaskan oil, traders said early Wednesday.
Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude for spot sales remained at a $1.70 discount to WTI, after nearly five days without sales.
ANS followed WTI's 20 cent fall, ranging $23.70/23.90 a barrel with some traders already gone for the holiday season.
Line 63 crude was thin, with no fixed basis deals and posted plus values stagnant at $0.95 to $1.05.
Kern River prices stayed $18.15/18.25 a barrel late after rising Monday on increased posted prices.
Discounts remained 10 cents below to even with postings, traders said.
Wilmington crude, produced offshore in Long Beach, Calif., also rose with postings Monday to $19.65/19.75.
